prose.text: {{right-to-left}} The navigation page's Findings and Users entries are crossed {{divergence:accessing-entries-crossed}}. See [[breach-predictor.tickets:jira-policy-tickets]] and [[breach-predictor.ai-assist:threat-summary]].

checks.do: When a severity score range or a score of 0 matters to an answer, give both ranges, 0 to 10 and 1 to 10, with the article for each, not one lower bound.

mapping-page.statement: The MITRE ATT&CK Mapping page can be filtered by attack stage (for example Discover Attack, Compromise, Lateral Movement and Data Loss), and by search for malware families or users; its table lists each malware family with a Threat column and a Severity Score column.

quotes: Filter by attack stage (e.g., Discover Attack, Compromise, Lateral Movement, and Data Loss).
Search for malware families or users in your organization to filter the results in the table.
Threat: The name of the malware family.
Severity Score: The threat score

severity-0-10.statement: In the MITRE ATT&CK Mapping table, the Severity Score is a threat score (0 to 10) assigned to each malware family by Zscaler ThreatLabz; the higher the score, the more damage the family can cause.

quotes: Severity Score: The threat score (0 to 10) assigned to each malware family by Zscaler ThreatLabz. The higher the score, the more damage a malware family can cause to your organization.

severity-1-10.statement: The Findings triage guidance says the severity score for each malware family ranges from 1 to 10 and is assigned by Zscaler ThreatLabz to indicate how much harm a malware family can do.

quotes: Focus on the severity score for each malware family: The score ranges from 1 to 10 and is assigned by Zscaler ThreatLabz to indicate how much harm a malware family can do to your organization.

possible-events.statement: Some events are identified as "possible", meaning they might have happened but were not captured as part of Breach Predictor's threat detection.

quotes: Some events are identified as "possible," meaning that they might have happened but were not captured as part of Breach Predictor's threat detection.

event-key.statement: On the Attack path tab, the Event key shows whether the threat's advancement to a technique is, for example, Observed, Possible or Predicted, and clicking Observed events shows specific information such as which URLs exposed users.

quotes: Use the Event key to determine the status of the threat's advancement to a particular technique (e.g., Observed, Possible, or Predicted).
You can click Observed events to see specific information (e.g., which URLs exposed users to the threat).

threat-page.statement: Clicking a malware family on the MITRE ATT&CK Mapping page opens its Threat page, where the Attack path tab includes a generative AI summary of the family and an Update Policy button for creating a Jira ticket.

quotes: When you click the name of a malware family on the MITRE ATT&CK Mapping page, the Threat page for the malware family opens.
On the Attack path tab, you can do the following:
See a generative AI summary of the malware family, including information about its lateral movement in your organization, recommendations for remediation, and information about any related threats.
Click Update Policy to see specific Breach Predictor recommendations for policy updates, and create a Jira ticket to update the policy.

events-tab-vs-page.statement: The Events tab on the Threat page shows nearly the same data as the Events page but focuses on a single threat, while the Events page covers multiple threats; the Events tab also provides more information about why particular policy updates are recommended, and Analyzing Findings describes it as the events for a particular time frame for a single threat as it relates to a single user.

quotes: The data presented on the Events tab is nearly identical to the data presented on the Events page.
the Events tab focuses on a single threat, whereas the Events page lets you look at data across multiple threats.
The Events tab also provides more information about why Breach Predictor is recommending particular policy updates.
Analyzing Data on the Events Tab
you see the events for a particular time frame for a single threat as it relates to a single user.

users-tab.statement: On the Threat page's Users tab, the Users view shows the most advanced MITRE ATT&CK technique either predicted or achieved by the malware family for each affected user; actual MITRE ATT&CK data is found in the attack path.

quotes: The Users view shows the most advanced MITRE ATT&CK technique either predicted or achieved by the malware family for each affected user.
To determine actual MITRE ATT&CK data, look at the attack path.

source-icons.statement: On the Attack path tab, for stages the threat family has achieved, the source of the threat data is shown by logo; the page's examples are the CrowdStrike logo for threats identified from CrowdStrike logs and the Zscaler logo for threats identified from Zscaler logs, and its list is open-ended ("e.g.", "etc.").

quotes: For stages that a threat family has achieved, you can see at a glance the source of the threat data (e.g., threats identified from CrowdStrike logs are identified by the CrowdStrike logo, threats identified from Zscaler logs are identified by the Zscaler logo, etc.).

triage-order.statement: The Analyzing Findings guidance for triaging malware families is: set a time period (starting small, then expanding), look for families at the far right of the matrix especially in Lateral Movement and Data Loss, start with higher severity scores, then work to reduce the total number of families.

quotes: Use the drop-down menu in the upper right of the Findings page to specify a time period for the data you see.
Scroll through the list of malware families and look for indicators that one has moved to the far-right side of the matrix
Start small to check more immediate threats and then expand the search.
focusing especially on the techniques in the Lateral Movement and Data Loss stages.
Start with the malware families that have higher severity scores.
work to reduce the total number of malware families affecting your organization.

stage-urgency.statement: As threats move to the Lateral Movement and Data Loss stages, quick action becomes more essential; an organization identified in the Data Loss stage is in danger of a data breach and must take action immediately.

quotes: as threats move to the Lateral Movement and Data Loss stages, quick action becomes more essential.
When your organization is identified as being in the Data Loss stage, you are in danger of a data breach and must take action immediately.

stage-discover.statement: Placement in the Discover Attack stage indicates that threat actors are surveilling the system by gathering information, scanning systems and developing resources to infiltrate the network.

quotes: Placement in the Discover Attack stage indicates that threat actors are surveilling your system by gathering information, scanning systems, and developing resources to infiltrate your network.

stage-compromise.statement: Placement in the Compromise stage indicates that threat actors have gained an initial foothold in the network and can execute code, persist, gain root access and evade detection.

quotes: Placement in the Compromise stage indicates that threat actors have gained an initial foothold within your network.
they can execute code, persist through attempted interruptions, gain root access, and use multiple methods to evade detection.

stage-lateral.statement: Placement in the Lateral Movement stage indicates that a threat actor is trying to gain account names and passwords, performing discovery on the network, and has begun to collect data; the organization is described as dangerously close to a full data breach.

quotes: Placement in the Lateral Movement stage indicates that a threat actor is actively attempting to gain access to account names and passwords, is performing different types of discovery on your network
has begun to collect data from your network and resources.
your organization is dangerously close to a full data breach.

stage-data-loss.statement: In the Data Loss stage, threat actors are trying to communicate with compromised systems, steal data, and control or destroy systems and data.

quotes: When your organization is identified as being in the Data Loss stage, you are in danger of a data breach and must take action immediately.
At this stage, threat actors are trying to communicate with compromised systems, steal data, and control or destroy your systems and data.

right-to-left.statement: The navigation page advises that, when working with Findings data, you should always work from right to left in the MITRE ATT&CK matrix; as a threat moves further to the right in the matrix, the organization is at a higher risk of a data breach.

quotes: As you work with Findings data, you should always work from right to left in the MITRE ATT&CK matrix; as a threat moves further to the right in the matrix, your organization is at a higher risk of a data breach.

severity-range.summary: The About Findings article (its MITRE ATT&CK Mapping Page section) gives the severity score range as 0 to 10, while the Analyzing Findings article gives it as 1 to 10.

positions.says: The Severity Score is a threat score from 0 to 10.

quotes: Severity Score: The threat score (0 to 10) assigned to each malware family by Zscaler ThreatLabz.

positions.says: The severity score ranges from 1 to 10.

quotes: The score ranges from 1 to 10 and is assigned by Zscaler ThreatLabz to indicate how much harm a malware family can do to your organization.

severity-range.impact: Whether a score of 0 is possible is unclear; do not state the lower bound of the severity scale as settled.

accessing-entries-crossed.summary: On the Accessing and Navigating page, the Findings entry ends with a pointer to About Users and the Users entry ends with a pointer to About Findings; the right-to-left Findings guidance sits under the Users entry.

positions.says: The Findings entry describes the Findings page, then points to About Users.

quotes: The Findings page provides an overview of the threats that are affecting your organization as a whole.
To learn more, see About Users.

positions.says: The Users entry describes the User Threat Profile page and carries the Findings guidance, then points to About Findings.

quotes: On the User Threat Profile page, you can view prioritized data across the MITRE ATT&CK matrix presented in the different tables.
To learn more, see About Findings.

accessing-entries-crossed.impact: Read the entries' text rather than their pointers or headings to tell which page is described; the right-to-left rule is Findings guidance either way.

evaluating-example-stage.summary: The Evaluating a Security Issue example places the Initial Access technique in the Discover Attack stage, while the same article's stage lists place Initial Access in Compromise.

positions.says: In the example, the smashbrowser family shows activity at Initial Access in the Discover Attack stage.

quotes: the smashbrowser malware family shows activity at the Initial Access technique in the Discover Attack stage.

positions.says: The Compromise stage includes Initial Access.

quotes: Initial Access
evidence.after: The Compromise stage includes these MITRE ATT&CK techniques:

evaluating-example-stage.impact: Use the stage lists, not the example's wording, to place a technique in a stage.

predicted-undefined.title: What the Predicted event status means
predicted-undefined.detail: The Event key lists Observed, Possible and Predicted, and Analyzing Findings speaks of Breach Predictor "predicting its advancement" of a technique and a threat "expected to move next"; but the captured articles define only Possible, and give no basis, confidence or timeframe for Predicted.

severity-scale-meaning.title: What specific severity score values mean
severity-scale-meaning.detail: The articles say a higher score means a family can cause more damage, but give no meaning for particular values or bands.
